plainText:
Aoi Yūki (Japanese: 悠木碧 Yūki Aoi) is a Japanese voice actress for .

==Biography==
Yūki was born on March 27, 1992, in , . She has played minor roles as a child actress in and TV series, before debuting as an anime voice actress in 2004, playing Marika from . Her first major voice acting role came when she was 16, when she played the seven-year-old Murasaki Kuhōin in .

Her former stage name was 八武崎碧 Aoi Yabusaki, the same as her real name, before changing it in 2007 when she transferred to the company Breath. In August 2008, she transferred to , with which she is still affiliated. Yūki also won both Best Leading Actress during the of 2012. She graduated from high school in March 2010 and university in March 2014.

==In the games==
===Generation VI===
====X and Y====
In Pokémon X and Y, Paulette on is named Aoi in the Japanese version, a possible reference to Aoi Yūki. This is supported by her use of an , which may represent Iris's Axew.

=====Pokémon=====
 
 
 
=====Quotes=====
Before battle
"“Dream big” is what I say! You’re looking at the future Champion, after all! Bring it on!"

Being defeated
"Wha-wha-what?! Perhaps that future-Champion stuff is all just a dream in the end..."

After being defeated
"OK. I’ll settle for being part of the Elite Four! OK. OK. I’ll settle for being a Gym Leader."
"But then again, I did say I should dream big... Got it! I’ll be the BEST Gym Leader in the world!"

====Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire====
 
Yūki appears in as the owner of a special Super-Secret Base in Mossdeep City that the player can visit after scanning a QR Code, which was first shown at the Pokémon Omega Ruby Alpha Sapphire Battle Streak Corner during Jump Festa 2015. The player can choose to challenge her to a Single Battle or invite her to their own Super-Secret Base. In-battle, she uses an that will always Mega Evolve at the first opportunity, as well as a , a Pokémon she portrayed in PK25.

Her team name is Team . Curiously, her Altaria has the move , despite its friendship value of 70 meaning that would have a higher base power.

Gameplay activity:
"I tried taking on the Pokémon League Champion for the first time a little while ago. I managed to win my way through, and it was all thanks to !"

===Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!===
 
In Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!, the Master Trainer is a named Aoi, referencing her role as the .
